item.title: Cops launch phase 2 of Carnival safety initiative
item.description: The Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) has launched phase two of Operation Festive Shield, under the theme: “Operation Secure De VIBES – Visibility, Intelligence, Border and Band Security, Enforcement, Safety for All.” In a media release on January 23, police said the initiative aligns with the national carnival theme for 2026: We Like It So. item.title: Woman sexually assaulted at Port of Spain school
item.description: Police are investigating the sexual assault of a woman in a lab at a secondary school in Port of Spain. item.title: No major damage after Jan 22 flash flooding
item.description: The rainfall on January 22 caused flash flooding in Barrackpore, Diego Martin, Cocorite, Penal/Debe and Port of Spain. Rural Development and Local Government Minister Khadijah Ameen said on January 23 there was no major impact as the waters subsided quickly. In a release on January 22, the ministry said it received reports of localised street and flash flooding in several areas following periods of heavy rainfall during the day. item.title: Pressure cooker thief arrested
item.description: A 20-year-old man has been arrested and is facing house breaking and larceny charges after stealing a pressure cooker and laptop from a house in Curepe. The 46-year-old victim locked the doors and windows of his apartment around 4.30 pm on January 21, and went away. On returning home around 7 pm, he saw the back door open. item.title: Condolences pour in for pregnant Venezuelan gunned down in Arouca
item.description: Venezuelans are mourning the murder of compatriot Yamerlis Lopez, originally from La Guaira in Sucre State, with tributes and condolences continuing to pour in on social media. After the fatal shooting on January 21 in Arouca, many Venezuelans shared messages describing her passing as an “unfortunate and irreparable loss,” offering sympathy particularly to her mother, Yaneisis, and her siblings. item.title: High Court appoints liquidator, Newsday’s 32-year run nears end
item.description: The High Court has approved an application to wind up the Newsday newspaper after 32 years. At a hearing on January 23, Justice Marissa Robertson granted an application filed on December 31 by attorneys for Daily News Ltd, the newspaper’s parent company. Justice Robertson also appointed chartered financial analyst Maria Daniel, a partner at Ernst & Young Services Ltd, as liquidator. item.title: Government announces end to STOW requirement
item.description: Minister of Energy Dr Roodal Moonilal announced on Thursday, the removal of the Safe To Work (STOW) Requirements for companies to enter the energy industry. Moonilal made the announcement at the post-Cabinet media briefing at the Diplomatic Centre. item.title: Migrant registrations start on Monday with background checks
item.description: The Migrant Registration Framework (MRF) has been fast-tracked and will officially begin on January 26, instead of January 30 as previously announced. At a post-Cabinet meeting on January 22, Homeland Security Minister Roger Alexander had announced that registration for all illegal migrants through the MRF would begin on January 30. item.description: Ultimate Soca Champion CEO Jerome "Rome" Precilla has confirmed that the competition will not be happening this year.
